answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using ephemeral cryptographic leases. Each node must periodically renew its registration by solving a resource-heavy puzzle cipher and publishing the proof to a distributed routing atlas. This forces an attacker to expend continuous memory bandwidth per active identity, as unmaintained credentials rapidly lapse into an inactive ember. However, network latency or transient packet loss can unfairly disenfranchise legitimate, lower-bandwidth agents.
